findings.title: FailedResolveDoesNotCount only exercises the expiry early-return, not the consume-last ordering
findings.failure_scenario: Move the ConsumeMemoShareView call in GetSharedMemo (memo_share_service.go:221) to just after getActiveMemoShare (line 183-186), before the memo fetch at line 188. An archived, SPACE-audience, unreadable or creator-missing memo then increments view_count and uses up the limit while returning NotFound. TestMemoShareViewLimit_FailedResolveDoesNotCount still passes, because its only failure is an expired share. isMemoShareExpired fails inside getActiveMemoShare (line 244) before any consume code runs.
findings.evidence: Test lines 480-487 set expires_ts in the past with raw SQL, then assert NotFound and ViewCount 0. memo_share_service.go:220 says 'Consume last so any failed resolve above leaves the count untouched', but no test reaches the later failure returns: line 193-194 (archived, missing or SPACE memo), line 197-198 (read context denied) and line 215-216 (creator not found). The pack's assumption says the view is consumed only after 'token found, not expired, memo readable'.
findings.fix: Add a case that creates a limited share, archives the memo (as TestGetSharedMemo_ReturnsNotFoundForArchivedMemo does), resolves it, and asserts NotFound and ViewCount==0 and ViewLimit remaining usable. Keep the expiry case too.
findings.verification_note: Traced GetSharedMemo. getActiveMemoShare returns NotFound for an expired share at line 244, before the memo fetch (188) and the consume (221). So the test cannot tell consume-last from consume right after getActiveMemoShare, and the suggested mutation would survive. The production code is correct today: consume runs after every check. The PLAN acceptance only asked for the expiry case, so the gap is in guarding a stated property, not a wrong outcome anyone sees. That is why I lowered it to minor under no-harm-yet: the reproduced impact is a regression the suite would miss, not a current failure.

findings.title: View-limit boundary values 1 and 1000 are never asserted as accepted
findings.failure_scenario: Change the check at memo_share_service.go:69 from `limit > 1000` to `limit >= 1000`. TestCreateMemoShare_RejectsViewLimitOutOfRange only tries 0, -1 and 1001, so it still passes, and a user asking for exactly 1000 views is rejected.
findings.evidence: Test line 418: `for _, limit := range []int32{0, -1, 1001}`. The accepted values elsewhere are 1 (line 431) and 5 (line 474). No test creates a share with 1000.
findings.fix: Add a positive case creating a share with ViewLimit 1000 and assert success and GetViewLimit()==1000.
findings.verification_note: Confirmed that service line 69 is `if limit < 1 || limit > 1000`. The lower boundary 1 is covered as accepted by TestMemoShareViewLimit_ResolvesOnceThenNotFound (line 431-435), so an off-by-one there would be caught. The upper boundary 1000 is never accepted in any test, so a `>= 1000` mutation survives. The current code is correct, so the severity stays minor under no-harm-yet. I moved the line to 418, which holds the value list; 417 is the func declaration. | reviewer cited line 417, verifier traced line 418

notes:
CreateMemoShare rejects view_limit outside 1..1000 with INVALID_ARGUMENT and stores it. GetSharedMemo calls Store.ConsumeMemoShareView(ctx, ms.ID) last, after memo conversion succeeds; false returns NOT_FOUND "not found". convertMemoShareFromStore sets ViewLimit and ViewCount. Tests: TestCreateMemoShare_RejectsViewLimitOutOfRange, TestMemoShareViewLimit_ResolvesOnceThenNotFound, TestMemoShareViewLimit_UnlimitedShareCountsWithoutLimit, TestMemoShareViewLimit_FailedResolveDoesNotCount.
